talks.title: Locked Down, Not Locked Out: How I Escaped Yr Secure Operator Workstation
talks.teaser: Locked Down, Not Locked Out: How I Escaped Yr Secure Operator Workstation — DEF CON Conference upload.
talks.summary:
In this operational case study from the DEF CON 33 ICS Village, an industrial penetration tester presents a practical methodology for escaping locked-down operator Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs) and engineering workstations in critical infrastructure facilities. Opening at 00:00, the speaker details the unique operational and safety constraints that govern security assessments in plant environments.

At 06:00, the presenter addresses common root causes of OT compromise, noting that default vendor credentials and over-permissive local group policies continue to plague industrial control systems. At 12:00, the talk explores human factors, warning that excessively restrictive workstation lockdowns often backfire by incentivizing operators to create insecure workarounds unless security teams build collaborative, blame-free relationships.

At 18:00, the speaker examines jump server and kiosk breakout techniques, demonstrating how unquoted service paths, unpatched helper utilities, and common file dialogs (such as triggering File Explorer through Help menus or print dialogs) enable testers to bypass kiosk restrictions. Concluding at 24:00, the session provides actionable hardening guidance for industrial defenders to isolate operator consoles without disrupting critical physical processes. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Crossing the Line: Advanced Techniques to Breach the OT DMZ
talks.teaser: Crossing the Line: Advanced Techniques to Breach the OT DMZ — DEF CON Conference upload.
talks.summary:
In this technical offensive briefing from the DEF CON 33 ICS Village, an OT penetration tester demonstrates advanced methods for crossing the boundary between corporate enterprise networks and industrial demilitarized zones (OT DMZs). Opening at 00:00, the speaker explains that compromising enterprise Domain Admin is rarely sufficient to impact physical processes due to strict perimeter firewalls and network segmentation.

At 04:01, the talk outlines the pivot workflow: testers locate dual-homed engineering workstations or operator accounts authorized to establish Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) sessions into the OT DMZ. At 08:00, the presenter demonstrates stealthy interaction using Hidden Desktop (HVNC) technologies, showing how operators can manipulate remote engineering consoles on isolated virtual desktops without alerting active operators on the physical screen.

Moving to detection analysis at 12:01, the speaker evaluates how defenders can identify anomalous inter-zone activity, comparing standard RDP sessions with hooked API calls. Concluding at 16:02, the presenter emphasizes that effective OT red teaming relies on living-off-the-land techniques rather than noisy C2 frameworks, urging blue teams to deploy strict application allowlisting and granular behavioral telemetry at OT perimeter firewalls. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)
